passage:
The movie theater changed from paper tickets to digital tickets. Customers only had to show a code on their phones.
Most people liked the change. It was faster and saved paper. But one afternoon, an old woman came alone and could not open her ticket. She had bought it with help from her grandson, but he was not with her.
A worker took her aside and helped her find the code. He also printed a small paper note with her seat number.
The theater later added a help desk for digital tickets.
New systems may be efficient, but they must still leave room for people who are learning. A good change should not make anyone feel locked outside.
